700: Bloody Sweet by NaRae Lee (Yen Press) is a full-color Korean romance with a gentle gothic edge. Naerim is an eighteen-year-old high schooler worn down by relentless bullying when she accidentally awakens Fetechou, a centuries-old vampire. He becomes an unexpected source of comfort, though he has his own reasons for staying close: her unusually powerful blood could help him become human again. It suits readers who like tender vampire romance with real emotional weight.
701: Portrait of M&N by Tachibana Higuchi (Tokyopop) is a lively shojo romantic comedy from the creator of Gakuen Alice. A high school girl hiding an embarrassing masochistic streak crosses paths with a handsome classmate who can't stop admiring his own reflection. Once they discover each other's secrets, the two form an awkward alliance to keep them hidden. It's light, silly fun for readers who enjoy offbeat school comedies and bickering, slow-building romance.
703: Absolute Duo by Shinichirou Nariie (Seven Seas) is an action fantasy set at a school for students with supernatural weapons. At Koryo Academy, students manifest Blazes, weapons drawn from their own souls, and Tooru Kokonoe is the odd one out when his Blaze takes the form of a shield. He is paired with Julie, a quiet transfer student from Northern Europe, as academy partners. It's a good fit for fans of battle-school stories with a touch of romance.
705: The Villainess Turns The Hourglass by Sansobee (Ize Press) is a full-color fantasy of second chances and revenge. Aria spent her first life as a scheming noble daughter, only to be outmaneuvered by her sweet-faced half-sister and sent to her death. When a mysterious hourglass sends her back in time, she resolves to play the game smarter and turn the tables. It's for readers who enjoy clever, determined heroines and satisfying palace intrigue.
706: The Knight Captain is the New Princess-To-Be by Yasuko Yamaru (Seven Seas) is a sweet fantasy romantic comedy. Christina, known as Lady Chris, was raised much like a boy and now serves as captain of the imperial guard, protecting her childhood friend, Prince Leonardo. When the king tells Leo to choose a wife, he announces he's already picked Chris, and she plays along, assuming it's all for show. It's a charming read for fans of fake-engagement romance and capable heroines.
707: Tengen Hero Wars by Yasu Hiromoto and Kubara Sakanoichi (Titan Manga) is a high-energy historical fantasy adventure. A modern teen named Oda Nobunaga, mocked for his obsession with history, is pulled into the past while trying to save his little sister, who is then taken by bandits. With no special powers, he has only his encyclopedic knowledge of historical figures to offer the warlord who shares his name. It's great for readers who love famous figures from Japanese history thrown together in big battles.
708: Plum Crazy! Tales of a Tiger-Striped Cat by Natsumi Hoshino (Seven Seas) is a gentle, all-ages comedy about life with cats. Plum is a tiger-striped cat living with the Nakarai family, sharing the household with other feline friends, including a mischievous kitten named Snowball. Short chapters follow everyday cat antics, naps, and small household adventures. It's a cozy pick for cat lovers and readers who enjoy warm slice-of-life stories.
709: It's All Your Fault by merryhachi (Yen Press) is a lively yuri comedy set in the world of cosplay. Shiho Kumai, a devoted manga fan and cosplayer, steps in to help a woman being harassed at her university, who turns out to be Yotogi, a popular cosplayer with a huge online following. After they team up at an event, Shiho learns that Yotogi's revealing style is exactly the kind of cosplay she dislikes. It's a fun pick for readers who enjoy fandom stories and sparky, mismatched pairs.
711: Psy Come by Mizuki Mizushiro (Yen Press) is a darkly comic action light novel. Kyousuke Kamiya is an ordinary teenager until he's wrongly convicted of murdering twelve people and shipped off to Purgatorium, a reform school for juvenile killers. Surrounded by classmates who really are dangerous, he just wants to survive and keep his head down. It's for readers who like twisted school settings, black humor, and over-the-top characters.
712: Telepathic Wanderers by Yasutaka Tsutsui and Sayaka Yamazaki (Tokyopop) is a psychological thriller with supernatural elements. Based on Tsutsui's novel Nanase Futatabi, it follows Nanase, a young woman who can hear other people's thoughts and has learned to keep her gift hidden. As she travels, she meets others with unusual powers of their own and learns how dangerous it can be to be found out. It's for readers who enjoy quiet, unsettling stories about psychic abilities.
713: StarCraft: Frontline by Various Authors (Tokyopop) is an anthology of science fiction manga set in Blizzard's StarCraft universe. Each volume gathers several self-contained stories from different creators, following Terran soldiers, Protoss warriors, and the ever-present Zerg threat. The tales range from frontline combat to smaller, character-driven moments in a galaxy at war. It's a natural fit for fans of the games and readers who like gritty military sci-fi in short doses.
714: Cells at Work! Baby by Akane Shimizu (Kodansha) is a cheerful educational comedy, drawn by Yasuhiro Fukuda, set inside the body of a newborn. The baby's cells are just as new to their jobs as the baby is to the world, and every hiccup, feeding, and first germ becomes a big event. Like the original series, it explains real biology through lovable, hardworking characters. It's a fun read for fans of Cells at Work! and curious readers of all ages.
715: I See Your Face, Turned Away by Rumi Ichinohe (Kodansha) is a bittersweet school romance from the creator of My Sweet Girl. It follows four teenagers and four stories of unrequited love, each watching the person they care about from a distance. They want to protect their friendships, but they can't stop hoping for something more. It's a lovely fit for readers who enjoy quiet, emotional romance like A Sign of Affection.
718: My Beautiful Man by Nagira Yuu (Yen Press) is a tender, intense boys' love romance. Hira is a quiet high schooler with a stutter who sits at the bottom of his class's social ladder. He becomes utterly devoted to Kiyoi, the aloof, beautiful boy at the very top, and the two begin an unlikely and complicated connection. It's for readers who like character-driven BL with plenty of emotional push and pull.
720: Tales of the Hundred Monsters Next Door by Yoshiko Watanuki (Seven Seas) is a gently eerie supernatural romance. Jinpachi Katagiri is a quiet book cover designer who likes his life predictable, until mysterious supernatural creatures start taking an interest in him. His strange encounters only multiply after he meets Oriza Harada, a writer known as "Ghost Sensei." Caught between his growing attraction to Harada and his wish for an ordinary life, Jinpachi finds his days anything but dull.
729: Lovely Muco! by Takayuki Mizushina (Kodansha) is a cheerful comedy about a dog and the person she adores. Muco is an energetic, endlessly affectionate little dog who lives in a small mountain town with her owner, Komatsu. Short, upbeat chapters follow her enthusiastic misadventures and her total devotion to her human, misunderstandings and all. It's an easy, feel-good read for dog lovers and fans of light slice-of-life humor.
730: The White Mage Doesn't Want To Raise The Hero's Level by Kirie (Seven Seas) is a playful isekai romantic comedy. Izumi Irie is summoned to another world as its hero and teams up with Sheena, a powerful white mage. Sheena has fallen for him and worries he'll be sent home once the Demon King is beaten, so she does everything she can to keep him distracted from leveling up. It's light, flirty fun with a healthy dose of fanservice.
733: Mii-Chan Wants To Be Kept by Waka Takase (Seven Seas) is a sweet, offbeat romantic comedy. Iori is worn out from work and still grieving his late pet cat when he takes in a stray black cat one night. The next morning, he finds a young woman in his apartment who calls herself Mii-chan and insists she's that very same cat. It's a cozy, funny read for anyone who enjoys quirky domestic romcoms and feline charm.
735: Centuria by Tohru Kuramori (Viz Media) is a dark fantasy adventure with a strong emotional core. Julian is a young boy who escapes a cruel past by stowing away on a ship, only to be discovered and made a slave himself. Among the enslaved passengers he finds an unexpected found family, especially a kind, pregnant woman named Mira. It's a gripping read for fans of grim, sweeping fantasy in the vein of Berserk and Vinland Saga.
738: Hima-Ten! by Genki Ono (Viz Media) is a lighthearted shonen romantic comedy. Tenichi Iemori is a hardworking sixteen-year-old who cleans houses part-time to help support his family. On the first day of his second year, he discovers that Himari Yoshino, the popular model who just transferred to his school, is the client whose wildly messy apartment he's been hired to clean. It's breezy fun for readers who enjoy secret-sharing romcoms with plenty of heart.
743: The Tale of a Little Alchemist Blessed by the Spirits by Yocco and Junsui (Seven Seas) is a cozy fantasy light novel about a fresh start. In her past life, Daisy was abandoned by her family after receiving the humble God Occupation of Maid. Reborn as a viscount's daughter, she fears history will repeat itself when she's named an Alchemist, but this time her loving family builds her a laboratory instead. It's a gentle read for fans of slow-life fantasy, found warmth, and crafting magic.
744: Futari Switch by Akira Hiramoto (Yen Press) is a body-swap comedy from the creator of Prison School. High schoolers Ichigo and Shinichi suddenly find themselves living in each other's bodies, with no idea why it happened or how to undo it. Juggling each other's friends, reputations, and secrets leads to plenty of chaos. It's a good fit for readers who enjoy Hiramoto's bold, over-the-top humor and expressive art.
745: The Tale of a Little Alchemist Blessed by the Spirits by Yocco, Asanaya, and Junsui (Seven Seas) is a sweet fantasy manga adapted from the light novel. Daisy's previous life ended in neglect after her family rejected her for receiving the God Occupation of Maid. Reborn as a viscount's daughter with the Alchemist occupation, she braces for the worst, only to find her new family eager to support her dreams. It's a warm pick for readers who love gentle, slow-life fantasy.
746: Isekai Samurai by Keigo Saito (Yen Press) is an action fantasy with a refreshingly unusual heroine. Ginko is a female samurai who survived the Battle of Sekigahara and has spent years searching for a warrior strong enough to give her an honorable death in battle. While praying for a worthy opponent, she's transported to a fantasy world where humanity is under siege by a Demon King's forces. It's a treat for readers who love sharp swordplay and a deadpan, single-minded lead.
748: Shinobi Undercover by Ippon Takegushi and Santa Mitarashi (Viz Media) is a shonen action comedy with a sweet romantic streak. Yodaka is a supremely skilled ninja who happens to have crippling social anxiety. He's assigned to secretly guard Aoi Mukai, a clumsy high school girl targeted by rogue ninja, which means blending into school life and learning to actually talk to people. It's a fun mix of slick fight scenes and awkward, heartfelt comedy.
750: Taika's Reason by Paru Itagaki (Viz Media) is a dark, unsettling drama from the creator of Beastars. In a Japan where science can turn animals into humans, Ao comes home to find her family's pit bull, Taika, standing over her father's body, and she chooses to hide the truth rather than let the dog be put down. When Taika is later humanized and can finally speak, the secret they share grows even heavier. It's for readers who like tense, morally tangled stories.
754: Ultimate Exorcist Kiyoshi by Shoichi Usui (Viz Media) is a shonen action comedy about demon hunting. Kiyoshi Harai lost his parents to demons as a child and grew into an incredibly powerful exorcist, though he is painfully shy. He's assigned to an outpost in Naraku City, hidden inside a Chinese restaurant, where he battles demons alongside his fellow exorcists. It's a great pick for readers who like big supernatural fights balanced with goofy humor.
760: Spacewalking With You by Inuhiko Doronoda (Kodansha) is a warm, quietly moving coming-of-age drama. Yamato Kobayashi is a high schooler struggling with school and his part-time job, drifting close to becoming a delinquent. Everything starts to shift when he befriends Keisuke Uno, an eccentric transfer student who lives by his own set of rules. It's a lovely pick for readers who enjoy heartfelt friendship stories about people who see the world a little differently.
761: Love at First Memory by Narumi Hasegaki (Kodansha) is a shojo romance with a mystery at its heart. After a car accident, heiress Mia Takanashi wakes up in the hospital with no memory of her past. Soon she's approached by four different young men, each claiming to be her fiancé. It's a fun, swoony read for fans of reverse-harem romance who also like a puzzle to solve.
764: My Noisy Roommate: The Roof Over My Head Comes With Monsters by Kaho Ozaki (Kodansha) is a lighthearted supernatural comedy with a dash of romance. Osuke is excited to live on his own, until he's kicked out of his new apartment on day one. A real estate agent offers him a better place with a few conditions, including sharing it with Nijio, a striking blond man who insists that ghosts are real and that Osuke is a magnet for them. It's a fun mix of spooky and sweet.
768: Betrothed to My Sister's Ex Light Novel by Tobirano and Mai Murasaki (Seven Seas) is a tender fantasy romance. Marie has spent her life neglected by parents who adore her sister Anastasia. On her birthday she slips away to the garden and meets Duke Kyros, who is drawn to her gentle nature, and a mix-up over names sends his proposal her way. It's a satisfying read for fans of Cinderella-style stories about a quiet heroine learning her own worth.
771: Spider-Man: Octo-Girl by Hideyuki Furuhashi and Betten Court (Viz Media) is a playful action comedy set in the Spider-Man universe. After a battle with Spider-Man leaves Doctor Octopus in a coma, he wakes up in the body of Otoha Okutamiya, a middle school girl in Tokyo, with his own mind still intact. The result is a funny, surprising twist on a classic Marvel villain. It's a fun pick for Marvel fans and readers who enjoy offbeat superhero stories.
772: The Mortifying Ordeal of Being Seen by mmk (Viz Media) is a playful school romantic comedy. After a seating change, classmates Ikezawa and Eguchi end up sitting side by side. When he can't help commenting on her snug blouse, she fires right back about his own neckline, and the two settle into a running game of teasing and flustering each other. It's a fun read for fans of push-and-pull romcoms like Teasing Master Takagi-san.
776: Drawing From Your Memory by Shiki Kawabata (Kodansha) is a moving time-slip story about grief, art, and love, from the creator of Switched. Mahoro is an award-winning manga artist whose hit series was built on ideas from the notebook of Yukishima, a high school manga club classmate who died months after they met. When she gets a chance to go back, she sets out to give him back his story and save his life. It's for readers who love bittersweet, emotional romance.
778: Digimon by Akiyoshi Hongo (Tokyopop) is a fun, kid-friendly adventure based on the hit anime. A group of kids at summer camp are suddenly swept away into the Digital World, a strange land full of creatures called Digimon. Each child is paired with a Digimon partner, and together they must work as a team to survive and find their way home. It's a nostalgic pick for longtime fans and a great choice for young readers.
780: Splatoon 3 Splatlands by Sankichi Hinodeya (Viz Media) is a bright, goofy gag comedy set in the world of Nintendo's Splatoon 3. Inklings and Octolings dive into the Splatlands for colorful turf battles, silly rivalries, and plenty of over-the-top antics. The chapters are short, punchy, and packed with nods to the game. It's a natural fit for young gamers and Splatoon fans of any age.
793: Sunbeams in the Sky by Monika Kaname (Yen Press) is a gentle shojo romance about starting over. Twin sisters Himari and Mio begin high school carrying a secret they're determined to keep hidden, and Himari is still struggling with fears from her past. As they grow closer to classmates Tsukiyono and Asaka, keeping that secret gets harder. It's a heartfelt read for fans of soft, emotional school romance with themes of healing.
797: Minami Nanami Wants to Shine by Yuki Yaku (Yen Press) is a romantic comedy spin-off of Bottom-Tier Character Tomozaki, drawn by Bana Yoshida with character designs by Fly. It centers on Minami Nanami, the cheerful, energetic classmate who wants to find a way to truly shine. As she takes on new challenges, she leans on Tomozaki's help to take herself seriously. It's a fun companion read for Tomozaki fans who want more of its bright supporting cast.
